description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), found probing the magic.t "%ENV store"
cluster of the blessed baseline.  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p46-env-undef.pl):

    no warnings;
    $ENV{PCLU} = undef;
    printf "defined=%d exists=%d\n",
       (defined $ENV{PCLU} ? 1 : 0), (exists $ENV{PCLU} ? 1 : 0);

  perl 5.40.3:  defined=0 exists=1
  PCL:          defined=1 exists=1

`defined $ENV{VAR}` is an everyday guard, and this flips it.

BOTH AGREE ON THE REST (same probe): `exists` is 1 in both, and a child process
launched afterwards sees the variable present with an EMPTY value in both
(`printenv PCLU` prints nothing and exits 0).  So the OS-level effect is right;
only the value perl's %ENV magic hands back on read differs.

ALSO PROBED AND CORRECT (scratch/p45-env-store.pl): storing a REF stringifies
it (`ARRAY(0x...)`, and `ref $ENV{X}` is false afterwards in both), and storing
a number round-trips.  So the general %ENV store path is right -- this is the
undef case only.

RELATION TO THE BASELINE: the magic.t 10-row cluster "ENV store:
encoding/downgrading and stringification of the stored value" (rows 184-189,
191-193, 195) is UNEXPLAINED in the s464ay Pass-3 clustering.  This probe does
NOT reproduce those rows -- they compare against magic.t's own mocked
addresses and wide-character values and need the file's context -- so treat
this as a NEIGHBOUR of that cluster, not its cause.  Someone closing the
cluster should probe the wide-character half separately.

FIX SHAPE (untried): find %ENV's store path and keep an undef value undef on
read-back while still writing an empty value to the environment.  Check it
alongside #1029 (%SIG's store magic does not qualify a bare handler name) --
both are "a magic hash's store does not do what perl's store magic does", so
look for a shared store seam before writing two fixes (CLAUDE.md rule 11).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `$ENV{X} = undef` leaves the hash value DEFINED ("") in PCL where perl keeps it UNDEF -- so `defined $ENV{X}` takes the opposite branch; both agree that the child process sees an empty value
